remarks.name: Swyx
remarks.role: achieve ambition with intentionality, intensity, integrity & insanity.
remarks.text:
a very primitive form of the near term multiagent agi future is setting up one thread to ping back once its done so you create an implicit kanban/waterfall graph of  dependent threads but each preserving their own work and agents

i can't wait to setup a proper ui for this pattern but you can hack it together in most koding agents of choice rn
remarks.translation: 近期的多智能体AGI未来，一种非常原始的形式是设置一个线程，在其完成后进行回传，这样你就创建了一个隐式的看板/瀑布图，由相互依赖的线程组成，但每个线程都保留自己的工作与智能体。我迫不及待想为这种模式搭建一个合适的UI，但目前你可以在大多数你选择的编码智能体中临时拼凑出这种方案。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Correct take. 99% of tokens in the world will get consumed in an enterprise context. 

They will be for writing code, combing through insane amounts of life sciences research, automating manufacturing, securing enterprises, detecting fraud, and thousands of other tasks like this that have significant economic value. This is both where the cost of AI can be most justified but also where the impact of parallel workers doing tasks on your behalf is most useful.

Even the agents that most impact consumers will often be wrapped up as just end to end services where the consumer doesn’t think about there being an AI system on the other end, like faster insurance or onboarding to a bank.

The key though is it’s going to take years for diffusion of agents across the economy because workflows have to re-engineered to incorporate AI, which is a complete change to how most work happens today. Anyone who’s expecting this to happen overnight should be updating their timelines.
remarks.translation: 观点正确。全球99%的算力消耗将发生在企业场景中。这些算力将用于编写代码、梳理海量生命科学研究数据、实现制造自动化、保障企业安全、检测欺诈行为，以及成千上万类似具有重大经济价值的任务。这既是AI成本最能被合理化的领域，也是并行工作者代你执行任务最能发挥效用的地方。即便是对消费者影响最大的智能体，也往往会被包装成端到端服务——消费者根本不会意识到另一端存在AI系统，比如更快捷的保险理赔或银行开户流程。关键在于，智能体在经济各领域的渗透需要数年时间，因为必须重新设计工作流程以融入AI，这将彻底改变当前大多数工作的运作方式。任何期待一夜之间实现变革的人，都应该调整自己的时间预期。

remarks.text:
How to use my new /human-review skill to edit HTML and Markdown files directly:

1. Tell Codex or Claude Code: “Install this: https://t.co/VDArIG0lxf”

2. Type “/human-review (your doc name)”

3. It’ll open a visual editor where you can edit and format text directly, resize images, and leave feedback for AI like comments in a Google Doc

4. When you’re done, click “Send to agent” and watch it apply all the updates

Use it to edit PRDs, landing pages, and more.

I know we all like making our agents work for us, but sometimes a “human review” is needed for that final 10% of polish :)

⭐ the skill on GitHub if you like it:  https://t.co/VDArIG0lxf
remarks.translation:
如何用我的新 /human-review 技能直接编辑 HTML 和 Markdown 文件：  
1. 告诉 Codex 或 Claude Code：“安装这个：https://t.co/VDArIG0lxf”  
2. 输入“/human-review（你的文档名称）”  
3. 它会打开一个可视化编辑器，你可以直接编辑和格式化文本、调整图片大小，并像在 Google 文档中那样给 AI 留下反馈意见  
4. 完成后，点击“发送给代理”，看着它应用所有更新  
用它来编辑 PRD、落地页等各种文档。我知道大家都喜欢让代理替我们干活，但有时候那最后 10% 的打磨，还是需要一次“人工审核” :)  
如果你喜欢这个技能，请在 GitHub 上给它加星：https://t.co/VDArIG0lxf

podcasts.originalTitle: Chai Discovery's Bitter Lesson: Drug Design Is Another Scaling Problem
podcasts.excerpt: 多数人将生物学视为一门定制化、杂乱无章的科学。Chai Discovery 联合创始人乔希·迈尔和马特·麦克帕特隆却将其当作工程问题来处理。他们论证，药物设计遵循着那条苦涩的教训：只要规模化数据、模型和算力，模型就能学到手工构建的流程根本无法捕捉的东西。成果实实在在：Chai-2 将从头抗体设计的命中率从不足 0.1% 提升到了 16%，把大海捞针式的搜索变成了更像配钥匙开锁的过程。乔希提出一个反直觉的观点：生物学比代码更容易验证，并解释了为什么目标应该是做更多而非更少的实验室实验。他们的赌注是：打造一个设计套件，将药物发现周期从九个月压缩到九天，并为制药行业赋能，而非与之竞争。主持人为红杉资本的帕特·格雷迪和索娜莉·辛格。 00:00 引言 01:52 从发现到设计 03:25 专…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Most people treat biology as a bespoke, messy science. Josh Meier and Matt McPartlon, co-founders of Chai Discovery, treat it as an engineering problem. They make the case that drug design obeys the bitter lesson: scale data, models, and compute, and the model can learn what a hand-built pipeline simply couldn't capture. The results are concrete: Chai-2 pushed de novo antibody design from a sub 0.1% hit rate to 16%, turning a needle-in-a-haystack search into something more like designing a key to fit a lock. Josh argues, counterintuitively, that biology is more verifiable than code, and explains why the goal should be more lab experiments, not fewer. Their bet: a design suite that collapses drug discovery from nine months to nine days, and arms the pharma industry rather than competing with it. podcasts.excerpt: 德高望重的科学家、AI 研究员于尔根·施密德胡伯博士被公认为该领域的先驱之一，他通过其实验室的工作，提出了当今 Transformer、LSTM 和递归自我改进背后的关键思想。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件，随着开源技术追赶封闭实验室的步伐，当今对 AI 数据中心的投资将迎来调整，而通往通用智能的道路在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非互联网数据。最后，他重新审视了主流的 AI 安全论点，并描绘了一幅自我复制的机器人社会最终殖民太阳系的宏大愿景。（0:00）引言（1:24）超人类 AI 还有多远？（2:27）ChatGPT 为何未让他感到意外（3:21）递归自我改进之路（9:01）AI 会起飞吗……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. podcasts.excerpt: 科技界最受瞩目的分析师之一本尼迪克特·埃文斯做客雅各布·埃夫隆的节目。对话围绕本尼迪克特的核心论点展开：将人工智能的规模与过往平台变革（互联网、移动互联网、个人电脑）相类比，在分析层面毫无意义；更具建设性的做法是，研究那些技术在经济层面的实际演进过程，从而推断人工智能的价值将沉淀在何处。他认为，这次真正的不同在于，我们不知道人工智能的物理或科学边界，而过往变革中这些边界至少是可预知的——正是这种不确定性，既催生了通用人工智能的狂热，也助长了末日论调，却无法解决任何实质问题。本尼迪克特深入剖析了为何能力仍呈锯齿状分布，这意味着使用场景同样参差不齐；为何编程凭借可规模化验证的特性，成为首个真正的企业级应用场景；以及为何大多数消费级和企业级应用场景，仍有待创业者去发明……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Benedict Evans, one of tech's most widely-read analysts, joins Jacob Effron. The conversation centers on Benedict's core thesis that comparing AI's scale to past platform shifts (the internet, mobile, PCs) is analytically useless, and that the more productive move is studying how those previous technologies actually evolved economically to reason about where AI's value will accrue. He argues the one genuine difference this time is that we don't know AI's physical or scientific limits, unlike past shifts where the boundaries were at least knowable, and that this uncertainty is what fuels both AGI hype and doomerism without resolving anything.
